newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish government could quit over taxes-ministers.
newsitem.headline: Polish government could quit over taxes-ministers.

text.p: Polish Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko told senators on Wednesday the government would resign if parliament pushed through a budget-busting tax cut.

"If the Sejm (lower house) proposals went through, the government...would resign because it would not be able to take responsibility for measures that are wrong from the economic point of view and irresponsible politically," Kolodko told a Senate committee.
Leszek Miller, cabinet chief of staff and a leader of the dominant Democratic Left Alliance party in the ruling coalition, said much the same at a news conference.

"If, due to a flawed tax scale, tax revenues will not be able to cover expenditure, threatening a larger budget deficit...there would be grounds for considering the government's resignation," Miller said.
The Democratic Left's coalition partner, the Peasant Party, unexpectedly joined the opposition in the lower house of parliament, the Sejm, on October 24 in a bid to reduce taxes on the low-paid.
The government had proposed cutting the tax levels on three existing income bands bands from 21, 33 and 45 percent to 20, 31 and 43 percent next year,
The Sejm voted for four bands, taxed at 17, 20, 33 and 45 percent.

The Democratic Left is trying to persuade the Peasants to reverse the vote when the bill reaches the Senate, but even so chances of the Sejm bill coming into force are slim because President Aleksander Kwasniewski has repeatedly signalled he would block or veto it if it passed the Senate.
Kwasniewski told private Radio Zet on Wednesday it was too early to talk of the government resigning as the tax bill had not been put to a Senate vote or come to him for signature.
He said he backed tax cuts, but only if they did not harm the economy, adding: "Therefore I will decisively oppose ideas which threaten to increase inflation and disrupt the economy."
The ex-communist Democratic Left and the Peasants look increasingly uneasy in their three-year-old coalition but have repeatedly drawn back from the brink of a complete break.

Kolodko said said it would be possible to finance a slightly higher deficit without boosting inflation, but the lower house's proposals would create a 3.6 billion zloty ($1.3 billion) gap, which would be impossible to finance. ($1=2.8090 Zloty)
